title: Bounded symmetric Gaussian channels have a universal fourth-chaos Fisher law

channel_law.seed_class: Let X be bounded, symmetric, centered and unit variance, let Z be an independent standard Gaussian, and set Y_t=sqrt(t)X+sqrt(1-t)Z for 0<t<1.
channel_law.mehler_expansion: Relative to the standard Gaussian phi, p_t/phi=1+sum_(n>=3) t^(n/2) E[H_n(X)]H_n/n!. Symmetry removes odd n, variance matching removes n=2, and E[H_4(X)]=kappa_4(X).
channel_law.score_expansion: The relative score satisfies grad log(p_t/phi)=(kappa_4(X)/6)t^2H_3+O_X(t^3) in Gaussian-weighted L2.
channel_law.cumulant_transport: The fourth cumulant is exact: kappa_4(Y_t)=t^2 kappa_4(X).
channel_law.scope_guard: Boundedness supplies the controlled Hermite remainder. The statement is a scalar weak-channel law; it is not a global exact Fisher optimizer, a field lower bound or a variational coefficient theorem.
